episodes.title: Ep11: Jason Fishman — A digital-marketing agency CEO weighs whether generative tools for copy, targeting and optimization are eroding or sharpening demand for specialized human oversight in equity-crowdfunding campaigns.

Ep9: Sheldon Poon — In performance marketing agencies, AI delivers returns not through creative generation but by enforcing the tracking discipline and attribution fixes most competitors neglect, turning platform algorithms into reliable revenue engines.
Ep12: Thor Hesselberg — A recruitment founder counters AI deepfakes flooding hiring pipelines by…

Ep10: Roddy de la Garza — A veteran real estate broker who trains AI on brokerage systems weighs what judgment, intuition, and human connection he refuses to delegate while seeking spiritual balance through daily mindwork.

Ep7: Vincent Rylan — Rylan’s novel Memoirs of the End renders the AI transition’s endpoint as intimate first-person accounts of lost agency and reconfigured meaning once superintelligence declares itself.

Ep8: Sameer Ranjan — A mining engineer turned AI builder weighs how platforms guiding career choice and soft skills can keep human judgment central when the models risk automating the decisions they claim to augment.

Ep5: John Capobianco — A network automation builder who turned early ChatGPT experiments into a production-grade ReAct agent now weighs how much human oversight and orchestration remain essential once agents handle intent, verification, and collaboration in regulated environments.

Ep6: Matt Davis — How a founder embedding AI agents into enterprise software delivery multiplies senior judgment across programs while preserving human gates, and what that shift does to accountability, quality, and the wider engineering workforce.
